paper.title: The OCB Authenticated-Encryption Algorithm (RFC 7253); OCB3 from Krovetz and Rogaway, 'The Software Performance of Authenticated-Encryption Modes', FSE 2011

program.how: written for ounce-core from the RFC 7253 section 4 pseudocode (HASH, OCB-ENCRYPT) and FIPS 197 AES (S-box computed by GF(2^8) inversion; AES-128/192/256); no third-party code copied. Encryption direction only
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: RFC 7253 Appendix A: the 16 (N,A,P,C) tuples under AES-128 key 000102..0f with 128-bit tags, all 16 ciphertext||tag values match
the 14 internal values the RFC prints for the last tuple (L_*, L_$, L_0, L_1, bottom, Ktop, Stretch, Offset_0, Offset_1, Offset_2, Offset_*, Checksum_1, Checksum_2, Checksum_*) match (14 of 14)
the 96-bit-tag tuple with key 0f0e..00 matches (1 of 1)

the long-loop test for all nine parameter sets (AES-128/192/256 x tag 128/96/64 bits): each of 384 encryptions builds a 22400/20864/19328-byte string that a final OCB-ENCRYPT authenticates, and the 9 outputs match (9 of 9)

expected_values_source.what: RFC 7253 Appendix A sample results, parsed mechanically from the fetched RFC text
expected_values_source.note: the vectors are data, copied as numbers. Values from the original CCS 2001 OCB paper (an earlier OCB version with different offsets) are not checked

negative_control: built with -DOCB_RB=0x86 (doubling constant 0x86 instead of 0x87), 8 of 40 values match and the program exits 1; check.sh reports NOT REPRODUCED
not_checked: OCB's security proofs, the patent/licence status, or any cryptanalysis
OCB-DECRYPT (not implemented; tag verification and the INVALID path are not exercised)
nonce lengths other than 96 bits, tag lengths that are not whole bytes, ciphers other than AES
OCB1 and OCB2 (the earlier algorithms of the 2001 and 2003 papers)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about any hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the sample values printed in RFC 7253 Appendix A for the inputs listed. It does not show OCB is secure.
